name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Hormuz largely shut; mines and attacks
summary: Iran says two tankers hit mines at Hormuz on 1 Nov; Black Sea drone attacks persist
state: Iran's IRGC said on 1 Nov that two oil tankers using an unauthorised route struck mines and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz; UKMTO separately reported a tanker hit by an unknown projectile that day. This follows tanker attacks on 30–31 Oct. Drones hit at least seven cargo ships off Romania and Bulgaria in October.
for_you: Shipping delays and higher freight and insurance costs feed through to fuel and goods prices. Mariners should follow UKMTO and flag-state guidance.
rubric_hit: Hormuz substantially closed with attacks on shipping = Alert

sources.title: News Beep — Two oil tankers explode after hitting mine in Hormuz Strait, IRGC says
Al Jazeera — Iran war live: Tankers hit in Hormuz; Trump again says conflict to end soon
gCaptain — Iran's IRGC Navy says tankers catch fire in Strait of Hormuz

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
